cases.title: Back-titration assay of an ester with excess hydroxide
cases.script:
# MO-006: Back-titration assay of an ester with excess hydroxide
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
add v1 ethyl_acetate 0.0005mol
react v1 saponification
inspect v1
titrate v1 HCl 0.1M 0.1mL until ph 8.5 max 150
inspect v1
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 NaOH 0.001mol
titrate v2 HCl 0.1M 0.1mL until ph 8.5 max 150
inspect
cases.original_forecast: For complete hydrolysis, the activated sample should consume about 0.0005 mol less strong acid than the base blank at an endpoint that mostly leaves acetate deprotonated.

original_criteria.criterion: Compare the blank-minus-sample delivered acid equivalents with the observed ester loss.
Correct for endpoint resolution and check that appreciable acetate protonation or incomplete hydrolysis does not bias the difference.

original_limitations: At pH 8.5 acetate is mostly, not perfectly, deprotonated.
Strong-base pool ownership and titrator direction handling must be confirmed at runtime.
cases.prerequisites: Integrated hydrolysis source, current artifact/API/browser acceptance and independently accepted original OR006 replay.
cases.additional_review: Reconstruct blank-minus-sample actual acid equivalents, including titrant solvent, endpoint step size and acetate protonation at8.5. Compare with actual ester loss; no rounded endpoint pass.

cases.title: Chromatographic tracking of an ester-hydrolysis intermediate
cases.script:
# MO-011: Chromatographic tracking of an ester-hydrolysis intermediate
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 ethyl_acetate 0.001mol
add v1 NaOH 0.0005mol
measure v1 chromatograph
inspect v1
react v1 saponification
measure v1 chromatograph
inspect v1
add v1 NaOH 0.0005mol
react v1 saponification
measure v1 chromatograph
inspect
cases.original_forecast: If the chromatograph recognises the relevant molecular pools, ester features should decrease and ethanol features increase as additional hydroxide permits further hydrolysis.

original_criteria.criterion: Relate peak identities to independently reported species inventories after each stage.
Do not compare raw areas as stoichiometric mole ratios unless response factors are provided; ionic acetate need not produce a comparable volatile peak.

original_limitations: Chromatographic retention and detector coverage are simplified and may omit ionic products.
The two named calls must consume the correct remaining substrate pools.
cases.prerequisites: Integrated hydrolysis source, current artifact/API/browser acceptance and independently accepted original OR006 replay.
cases.additional_review: Verify successive0.5mmol named conversions spend remaining ester once. Independently identify ester/ethanol peaks and preserved unsupported ionic acetate; peak area is not mole fraction.

cases.title: Hydrolyse an ester, then oxidise the liberated alcohol
cases.script:
# MO-003: Hydrolyse an ester, then oxidise the liberated alcohol
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
seal v1 250mL
add v1 ethyl_acetate 0.001mol
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
react v1 saponification
inspect v1
add v1 O2 0.002mol
react v1 alcohol-oxidation
measure v1 ph
inspect
cases.original_forecast: Successful sequential transformations first yield acetate and ethanol, then convert the ethanol fraction into another acetate/acetic-acid family pool. Carbon accounting should retain four carbons per initial ester molecule.

original_criteria.criterion: Verify ethanol appears after hydrolysis and decreases only after the requested oxidation.
Sum carbon across molecular and ionic pools without double-counting mirrored aqueous representations.

original_limitations: Each stage may expose a molecular-versus-aqueous ownership boundary; available oxygen includes the headspace.
Formal product acid/acetate proportions depend on the actual proton balance.
cases.prerequisites: Integrated hydrolysis source, current artifact/API/browser acceptance and independently accepted original OR006 replay.
cases.additional_review: SOURCE-DOMAIN BLOCKER: sealing traps CO2, while the current hydrolysis admission excludes every carbonate/CO2 reservoir. Do not ignore air carbon or change the original boundary. First prove an expanded analytical-reserve contract and atomic controls; oxidation also needs available oxygen including trapped air. This is a static-source inference, not a new original-protocol execution.

cases.title: Sweeping ammonia changes the composition of a basic buffer
cases.script:
# AB-031: Sweeping ammonia changes the composition of a basic buffer
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 NH4Cl 0.001mol
add v1 NH3 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 NH4Cl 0.001mol
add v2 NH3 0.001mol
seal v2 100mL
measure v1 ph
measure v2 ph
sweep v2 1bar
wait 120s
measure v1 ph
measure v2 ph
inspect
cases.original_forecast: Selective NH3 removal should deplete the base component and lower pH relative to the sealed control; the ammonium/chloride reservoir is not itself a gas.

original_criteria.criterion: A pH decrease is accompanied by a documented loss of nitrogen through the gas boundary.
Chloride remains retained and is not confused with volatile NH3.

original_limitations: The sweep is an ideal boundary, not a specified physical gas-flow apparatus; NH3 transfer coverage must be checked.
cases.prerequisites: Ammonia artifact/API/browser acceptance and independent original GS005 replay; sweep remains its own boundary model.
cases.additional_review: Own all per-vessel elapsed histories because globalwait advances both controls. Close nitrogen using actual swept exports, retain chloride and NH4 pools, compare pH with sealed control; finite-headspace improvement alone does not validate sweep.
